claims: NASA is targeting an April 1, 2026, launch date for the Artemis 2 mission.
The Artemis 2 mission will send four astronauts on a 10-day trip around the Moon.
The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion spacecraft were rolled back to launch pad 39B in March 2026 for final preparations following repairs.
Potential backup launch dates are available in early April.
The mission goal of Artemis 2 is the first crewed flight of the SLS rocket and Orion capsule around the Moon.
The crew of Artemis 2 consists of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The launch site for Artemis 2 is Kennedy Space Center, Florida, Pad 39B.
The SLS rocket has returned to launch pad 39B as of March 20, 2026, for final tests.
If the primary April 1, 2026, launch date is missed, subsequent opportunities exist later in the month.
